gaps.note: The reader knows binary representation but not bit-reversed ordering or the bit-reversal permutation. The page neither explains it nor links it to another page, yet the level structure depends on it.

gaps.quote: a block of size $h$ computes a transform with root $\omega^{n/h}$ from two halves
gaps.note: The page asserts that a bit-reversed block of size h computes a transform with root omega^{n/h} from two half-size transforms with root omega^{2n/h}. It gives no derivation or link, and the reader cannot check it from the page.

gaps.quote: The split above, with $\omega^{n/h}$ in place of $\omega$, pairs offsets $t$ and $t+h/2$ into a butterfly with exponent $s=tn/h$.
gaps.note: The split was derived for omega with omega^{n/2} = -1. Applying it to omega^{n/h} needs omega^{n/h} to be a primitive h-th root with (omega^{n/h})^{h/2} = -1. The page never states this, so the substitution and the exponent s = tn/h cannot be checked from the page.
The claim that the level sequence yields the outputs in natural order, after bit-reversed input, is not justified or linked. The reader cannot check it from the page.

gaps.quote: Each level is one rearrangement that makes partners $t$ and $t+h/2$ adjacent, then one scan of butterflies.
gaps.note: The page asserts that a single address rearrangement makes every pair of partners adjacent at each level. It does not say which rearrangement or why it suffices, so the reader cannot check this claim from the page.
